docRequirement: mcp.md:108 binds the client side of MCP roots: "Claude Code answers `roots/list` with the session's launch directory plus every additional working directory you've granted with `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or the `additionalDirectories` setting" and "Claude Code sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes." The preceding sentence makes this the designated mechanism rather than an extra: "A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP `roots/list` request instead" (instead of reading `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`). So our MCP client must declare the `roots` capability with `listChanged`, serve `roots/list` with launch dir + additional working directories, and emit `notifications/roots/list_changed` on every change to that set.
current: Nessy never exposes MCP roots to any server, on any transport, for any backend. (1) Capability: packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 constructs `new Client({name:'nessy-agent',version:'1.0.0'}, { capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {} })` — the capabilities value is an either/or ternary with no accumulator, and `roots` appears in neither branch. (2) Handler: the only request handler registered on that client is `ElicitRequestSchema` (client.ts:325-343); the notification handlers are elicitation-complete plus tools/resources/prompts list-changed (client.ts:346-360). No `ListRootsRequestSchema` handler exists, so a server that sent `roots/list` anyway would get 'Method not found'. (3) Notification: `sendRootsListChanged` is never called. (4) Absence is repo-wide and NUL-safe: `grep -ran "roots/list\|ListRootsRequestSchema\|listRoots\|sendRootsListChanged\|RootsListChanged" packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` exits 1 with zero hits. (5) Nothing adds it later — the repo's only `registerCapabilities` is `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/capabilities.ts:89`, an unrelated RPC-handler registrar in a sibling subsystem, not an MCP capability registration. (6) The two sibling MCP clients omit roots too: packages/shared/src/mcp/api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument; packages/shared/src/mcp/validation.ts:411-413 passes `{ capabilities: {} }`. (7) The consequence reaches every backend because Nessy's own pool is the sole client that connects third-party servers: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1136 builds each `NessyMcpClient` with only `elicitationHandler`/`channelServer`/`pluginProcessAuthority`, and packages/shared/src/mcp/pool-server.ts:210-213 re-exposes that same pool to Pi/Codex as a SERVER (`nessy-pool-proxy`, `capabilities: { tools: { listChanged: true } }`), so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path. (8) The SDK is ready and asserts on our omission: node_modules/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/dist/esm/client/index.js:621 exposes `sendRootsListChanged()`, :394 throws unless `_capabilities.roots.listChanged` is set, :427 throws unless `_capabilities.roots` is set. (9) Both inputs the doc names already exist server-side of us: the launch-directory analogue is the pool's `workspaceRootPath` (mcp-pool.ts:578, :643, :685; resolved at packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:245 and passed at :790), and the additional-directory list is the persisted `additionalDirectories` setting (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:132, packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:191 and :227) canonicalized into a `roots: string[]` by packages/shared/src/agent/additional-directories.ts (`resolveAdditionalDirectories`, `getConfiguredAdditionalDirectories`), already unioned with the session-scoped `addDirectories` grant by packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2711-2717 over packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:3193-3212. (10) The current capability surface is pinned by test: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:79-90 asserts `sdkClient._capabilities.elicitation` equals `{form:{},url:{}}` with a handler and that the capabilities object is otherwise empty without one.
divergence: The entire client-side roots surface is missing — this is not a wrong key name or a narrowed value. Three distinct absences: the `roots` client capability (with `listChanged: true`) is never declared at the MCP handshake; no `roots/list` request handler is registered, so the method does not exist on our client; `notifications/roots/list_changed` is never emitted. The data the doc says to answer with is already computed and correct in this repo (workspace root + `additionalDirectories` + session `addDirectories` grants) — it simply has no path to the MCP wire. Secondary structural delta: Claude Code has one MCP client per session, so its roots are per-session; Nessy's pool is shared per (workspaceId, projectKey) and leased by sessions (workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:165-166, :201-230), so one connection cannot answer differently per session — a decision the implementation must make explicitly rather than inherit.

change.what: Add constructor option `rootsProvider?: () => readonly string[] | Promise<readonly string[]>`. Rewrite the capabilities argument at :310-324 from the either/or ternary into an accumulated object — `{ ...(options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}), ...(options?.rootsProvider ? { roots: { listChanged: true } } : {}) }` — because a naive key append to the current ternary would drop elicitation in one branch. When `rootsProvider` is present, register `this.client.setRequestHandler(ListRootsRequestSchema, async () => ({ roots: (await provider()).map(p => ({ uri: pathToFileURL(p).href, name: basename(p) })) }))` (import `ListRootsRequestSchema` from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js', `pathToFileURL` from 'node:url'); the MCP `Root.uri` must be a `file://` URI, not a bare path. Add a public `async notifyRootsChanged(): Promise<void>` that no-ops unless connected and the capability was declared, then calls `this.client.sendRootsListChanged()` (the SDK throws otherwise — dist/esm/client/index.js:394). Add `notifyRootsChanged?(): Promise<void>` as an OPTIONAL member of the `PoolClient` interface at :234-255 so `ApiSourcePoolClient` (in-process API sources, which need no roots) stays conformant unchanged.

change.symbol: McpClientPool constructor options + connect() + a new notifyRootsChanged()
change.what: Add `rootsProvider?: () => readonly string[] | Promise<readonly string[]>` to the options bag at :641-683 (next to `workspaceRootPath` at :643) and store it at :685. Pass it through at :1136 into `new NessyMcpClient(clientConfig, { ... })`. Add `setRootsProvider(provider)` and `async notifyRootsChanged()` that fans out over `this.clients` calling each client's optional `notifyRootsChanged()`, swallowing per-connection errors the way `emitToolsChanged`/the channel dispatcher already do. Do NOT have the pool read config itself: the existing comment at :676-681 records that 'the pool has no settings layer of its own', so the provider is injected, matching how `wsNetworkPolicy` is handled.

Supply the provider at :790 alongside the existing `workspaceRootPath` spread: `rootsProvider: () => [workspaceRootPath, ...getConfiguredAdditionalDirectories()].filter(Boolean)` (import from '@nessy-agent/shared/agent'; `getConfiguredAdditionalDirectories` is already memoized on the raw config entries — additional-directories.ts:70-80 — so a settings edit takes effect without a restart and the provider needs no cache of its own). Decide and record which set a SHARED pool answers with: the workspace-level union is the simplest correct answer and is a superset of any single session's launch directory, but it means a session-scoped `addDirectories` grant widens the roots reported to servers other sessions in the same workspace are also using. Expose a registry-level `notifyRootsChanged(key)` that forwards to the leased pool so the two change sources below have something to call.

After `this.sessionAdditionalDirectories` actually changes, signal the pool so `notifications/roots/list_changed` goes out — this is the 'when that set changes' half of mcp.md:108 for the mid-session path. Use the existing injected pool handle rather than importing the pool here; if none is reachable from this class, raise the signal to `SessionManager.sessionAdditionalDirectories` (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2711-2717), which is already the single union reader and does hold the lease. The other change source is a write to the `additionalDirectories` setting (config/storage.ts:132) — notify from that save path too. Emit at most one notification per change, and none when the resolved union is byte-identical.

The two existing assertions read `sdkClient._capabilities` and must be updated: with a `rootsProvider` the object now also carries `roots: { listChanged: true }`, and the 'advertises no elicitation capability without a handler' case must keep asserting `elicitation` is undefined while roots may be present. Add: (a) `_requestHandlers.has('roots/list')` is true only when a provider is supplied; (b) the handler returns `file://` URIs for launch dir + additional dirs; (c) `notifyRootsChanged()` is a no-op without the capability and does not throw (the SDK would).

blastRadius: CROSSES A WIRE BOUNDARY — a risk trigger in this repo. The client `capabilities` object is sent in the MCP `initialize` handshake to every third-party server on every transport (stdio, http, sse, ws — client.ts:371-425), so this changes what every connected server sees at connect time, adds a new inbound request method (`roots/list`) and a new outbound notification. It also crosses a data-egress boundary that did not exist before: `roots/list` discloses absolute local filesystem paths to every connected server, including REMOTE http/sse/ws servers that previously received none. Callers and readers: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1136 is the sole production constructor of `NessyMcpClient`; the `PoolClient` interface (client.ts:234-255) is implemented by `ApiSourcePoolClient` (api-source-pool-client.ts:15) and consumed throughout the pool, so the new member must stay optional; packages/server-core/src/mcp/workspace-mcp-pool-registry.ts:789 is the sole production pool factory, and the pool is keyed per (workspaceId, projectKey) and shared across session leases (:165-166, :201-230). Downstream of the pool, packages/shared/src/mcp/pool-server.ts:210-213 re-exposes the pool to Pi and Codex as `nessy-pool-proxy`; it is a server, not a client, so it is unaffected unless a later change forwards roots through it. Tests that pin the touched surfaces: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:65-120 (capabilities and handler registry), and the pool suites under packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/ (proxy-tool-names.test.ts, runtime-pool-servers.test.ts) construct raw SDK clients and pools. No persistence boundary is crossed: the roots answer is derived at request time from `workspaceRootPath` plus the already-persisted `additionalDirectories`; nothing new is written to disk. Imported-plugin path: plugin-provided MCP servers connect through the same pool (`pluginRuntime` branch at client.ts:373-380), so they gain roots along with native and project servers.
userImpact: Latent for most users today, and concretely broken for one class of server. A user connects an MCP server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots (the pattern mcp.md:108 explicitly routes servers to): the server's `initialize` response shows a client with no `roots` capability, so it never asks, falls back to its own default — typically nothing, or an operator-configured allowlist — and its file tools then either refuse ('no accessible roots' / 'path not allowed') or operate on the wrong directory. In the Sources surface such a server connects and lists tools normally, so nothing looks wrong; the failure appears only when a tool is called. Second, invisible-by-construction effect: a user who adds a working directory mid-session (the `addDirectories` grant path, pi-agent.ts:3193) or edits `additionalDirectories` in settings gets no `notifications/roots/list_changed`, so even a server that had roots would keep the stale set for the life of the connection. What would make it surface broadly: any commonly installed server adopting roots-based scoping — the mechanism is client-advertised, so adoption on the server side alone turns this from latent into a visible tool failure with no diagnostic pointing at us.
